chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Chicago union welcomes McRae
summary: Returning east through Chicago, the Black local's officers and some fifty members came to greet him.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

blocks.x: So eventually you come back to the east coast.
When we came back to the east coast --
When we came back to the east coast, we had played -- we came back through Chicago. Oh this will floor you.
We came back to Chicago and we had

played the theater, right? Now we come back to Chicago, we play in the Savoy Ballroom.
And when I get to the Savoy Ballroom, I see all these musicians dressed in tuxedos and everything -- they looked good. They were all standing over there in the corner to the right of the bandstand.

And I'm thinking about the (inaudible), pianist playing you know. And intermission, these fellas -- president of the union (inaudible), walks in he says, "Welcome to Chicago. We want to welcome you to Chicago, I've been hearing about you, we love your playing and everything."
He (inaudible) welcomed me -- you know, give me a big send off and everything.
They wanted me to come down to the union the next day. They had a luncheon for me and everything.
That was the colored union. That's before they merged into the white union.
And it was a real wonderful thing. I say, "Great, wonderful," you know.
